source.anchor: Chen-Chewi-Lu-Zhang arXiv2609.06905v1 Appendix A.1 (A.1),(A.2), strict finite-prefix iteration ingredient of (A.7), and Appendix A.2 joint Borel construction; attributed ASTIS completion.
source.original_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ with α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. Fix any deterministic y,r∈E and initial phase z₀∈E×E. Put c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}, Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Total real division makes S_r the identity at g_r(x)=0. The record space is D=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊕{stopped}, with Borel sum structure. Define next(e,stopped)=stopped; for a live record (T,z), next(e,(T,z))=stopped if τ_z(e)=∞, and otherwise next(e,(T,z))=(T+τ_z(e),S_rΦ_(τ_z(e))(z)). In the Lean definition untopD0 is used only in this non-top branch. Define R₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and R_(j+1)(e)=next(e_j,R_j(e)). Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ with its product Borel structure and P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1). Let ε(w)_k=max{w_k,0}; this is an ambient coordinate extension on a P-null nonpositive-clock set, not new source dynamics for negative clocks. For every deterministic finite n≥0 and finite horizon T≥0, let Hist_n=D^(Fin(n+1)) and H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_(0≤j≤n). Write rtime(live(a,z))=a and rtime(stopped)=0. Define the measurable ordered simplex Δ_n(T)={t∈ℝ^n:0<t_1<⋯<t_n<T}; its subtype carries m_n, the comap of product Lebesgue volume along inclusion. For t∈Δ_n(T), put s_0=0,s_i=t_i, z_0=z₀ and z_i=S_rΦ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1)) for 1≤i≤n. Define K_n(t)_j=live(s_j,z_j). Define qReal_n(t)=∏_(i=1)^n [λ_r(Φ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1))) exp(−Λ_(z_(i−1))(s_i−s_(i−1)))] and q_n=ofReal(qReal_n). Here the literal Lean definitions use toNNReal on times and elapsed times; these agree with the displayed nonnegative values on the simplex. Let A_n(T) be the abstract-history set in which all n+1 records are live, their read times are strictly increasing, and each postinitial read time is below T. A_n(T) does not itself constrain the initial record time. Set B_n(T)=H_n^(-1)(A_n(T)) and obs_n(w)_i=rtime(H_n(w)_(i+1)); actual H_n(w)_0 is always live(0,z₀). Then Δ_n(T) and A_n(T) are Borel. For fixed n,T, K_n and q_n are jointly Borel in (y,r,z₀,t). For every y,r,z₀, H_n,obs_n and B_n(T) are Borel, and qReal_n(t)≥0 for every simplex point. For every raw w∈B_n(T), there exists t∈Δ_n(T) with t=obs_n(w) and H_n(w)=K_n(t), as complete tagged histories. The exact unnormalized law is (H_n)_*(P restricted to B_n(T))=(K_n)_*(q_n m_n). For every Borel F:Hist_n→[0,∞], ∫_(B_n(T))F(H_n(w))P(dw)=∫_(Δ_n(T))F(K_n(t))q_n(t)m_n(dt). Moreover ∫q_n dm_n=P(B_n(T))≤1. This includes n=0,T=0, zero hazard and extended-valued tests; there is no boundedness, integrability or positive-event-mass assumption. This is the strict first-n-prefix law, without a final survival factor, and is not a raw exact-n event-count law. It is an attributed ASTIS completion of the finite ordered iteration ingredient implicit in Appendix A.1(A.7), with joint Borel construction from Appendix A.2. The dimension-zero and ENNReal-test extensions are explicit ASTIS extensions. Terminal survival, endpoint/count identification, the full path-functional A.7 expansion, restart/Markovness, invariance, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected costs and full paper/composition remain outside this result.

lean.statement:
{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let rate : E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun xRef z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>
      ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), rate xRef (Φ y xRef s z)
    let τ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → WithTop ℝ≥0 := fun y xRef z e =>
      MeasureTheory.hittingAfter
        (fun t : ℝ≥0 => fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × ℝ≥0 =>
          Λ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 t - (a.2.2 : ℝ))
        (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0 ((y, xRef), z, e)
    let next : E → E → ℝ≥0 → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) →
        ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef e r =>
      match r with
      | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ()
      | Sum.inl a =>
        if τ y xRef a.2 e = ⊤ then Sum.inr () else
          Sum.inl (a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0,
            S xRef (Φ y xRef (((τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2))
    let record : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ →
        ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
      Nat.rec (Sum.inl (0, z₀)) (fun k r => next y xRef (e k) r) n
    let P : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ))
    let ε : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 := fun w k => Real.toNNReal (w k)
    let history : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (ℕ → ℝ) →
        (Fin (n + 1) → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit)) :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n w j => record y xRef z₀ (ε w) j.val
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let readTime : Rec → ℝ := fun r => match r with
      | Sum.inl q => (q.1 : ℝ)
      | Sum.inr _ => 0
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let qReal : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ∏ i : Fin n,
        rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
          (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)) *
        Real.exp (-Λ y xRef (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)
          (Real.toNNReal (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)))
    let q : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (qReal y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let A : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Hist n) := fun n T =>
      {h | (∀ j, ∃ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), h j = Sum.inl a) ∧
        StrictMono (fun j => readTime (h j)) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin n, readTime (h i.succ) < (T : ℝ)}
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0,
      MeasurableSet (Δ n T) ∧ MeasurableSet (A n T) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        K p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        q p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E,
        let H : (ℕ → ℝ) → Hist n := history y xRef z₀ n
        let B : Set (ℕ → ℝ) := H ⁻¹' A n T
        let obs : (ℕ → ℝ) → Fin n → ℝ := fun w i => readTime (H w i.succ)
        Measurable H ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧ Measurable obs ∧
        (∀ t : Prefix n T, 0 ≤ qReal y xRef z₀ n T t) ∧
        (∀ w ∈ B, ∃ t : Prefix n T, t.val = obs w ∧ H w = K y xRef z₀ n T t) ∧
        Measure.map H (P.restrict B) =
          Measure.map (K y xRef z₀ n T) ((m n T).withDensity (q y xRef z₀ n T)) ∧
        (∀ F : Hist n → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable F →
          (∫⁻ w in B, F (H w) ∂P) =
            ∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, F (K y xRef z₀ n T t) * q y xRef z₀ n T t ∂m n T) ∧
        (∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, q y xRef z₀ n T t ∂m n T) = P B ∧
        P B ≤ 1)
decoder_context: All displayed functions are literal definitions on a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero. fderiv is Frechet derivative, gradient the inner-product gradient, and ContDiff real2 twice continuous differentiability.
expMeasure1 is the rate-one exponential law on real numbers; infinitePi is its canonical countable product. Real.toNNReal is max(x,0) represented as a nonnegative real.

WithTop NNReal includes infinity. hittingAfter is the infimum of nonnegative entry times, infinity if none exists. untopD0 returns the finite value with default zero at infinity. Sum.inl/inr are distinct Borel tags; Unit is a singleton; products associate right.
Fin(n+1) indexes0 through n. Fin.snoc h a appends a as the last coordinate and keeps all earlier coordinates. j.castSucc embeds an old Fin index in the larger tuple with the same value.

Measurable is Borel measurability. Measure.map is pushforward, restrict is unnormalized measure restriction, withDensity multiplies the reference measure by the indicated nonnegative density. Real volume is Lebesgue measure.

Real division is total with division by zero equal to zero. Interval integrals are real Bochner integrals; Nat.rec is the displayed finite recursion; ENNReal.ofReal embeds max(x,0). Nonnegative extended Lebesgue integrals need no integrability premise.
Fin.cons inserts its first argument at index zero; Fin.induction is recursion on a finite ordered index. StrictMono means strict order preservation, and finite products over Fin0 equal one.
The finite function-space volume is the product of real Lebesgue measures. Measure.comap along Subtype.val gives the measure on that measurable subtype; it is not a normalized probability measure.
